text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Health Minister Jacques Barrot defends government's draft bill on "social unity", adds government will not consider altering planned social security reforms.
-- First half profits for SGS Thomson fell by half from same period last year.
-- TPS digital-TV aims for 300,000 subscribers at end 1997.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Drought threatens two-thirds of French territory.
-- Analysts skeptical over target presented by Suez- Lyonnaise des Eaux to double profits per share in a five-year period.
-- Casino managing director Yves Martin to replace Henri de Bodinat as head of marketing and sales at Club Mediterranee.
L'AGEFI
-- Fortis AG chairman Maurice Lippens says aims of French government are not yet clear regarding a possible sale of insurer GAN, adds group seeks external growth.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- CFDT union leader Nicole Notat says union has over 700,000 members, a signal of approval of her strategy.
-- Businessman Edouard Stern may be about to leave Lazard Frere.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Exports of French wine boosted by reports about its positive effects on health.
-- Work resumed at Renault Vilvoorde plant on Monday.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- SGS-Thomson shares fall four percent as profit skids.
